think:
1. Core Clinical Tension: A 21-year-old woman presented with a 6-year history of recurrent purulent discharge from two sinus openings on the right breast without constitutional symptoms, palpable breast lumps, or axillary lymphadenopathy. Primary mammary tuberculosis is exceedingly rare (<0.1% of breast lesions) and commonly mimics pyogenic breast abscess, chronic suppurative mastitis, or breast carcinoma with fistulization. Moreover, the purulent aspirate from the breast sinus was sterile on direct mycobacterial smear. The underlying disease was actually secondary contiguous extension from an occult tuberculous osteolytic lesion of the underlying fifth rib.
2. Admission Breakpoint: Admission triage terminates after documenting the 6-year history of discharging breast sinuses, physical examination (normal left breast, right breast sinus draining whitish pus with adjacent scar, palpable firm tracts ending on the fifth rib, absence of breast lump or axillary adenopathy), elevated ESR, and positive Mantoux test (16x14 mm), immediately prior to imaging of the chest wall, sterile aspirate analysis, and surgical rib resection.
3. Differential Distinctions: Chronic pyogenic breast abscess / suppurative mastitis was suspected given chronic purulent discharge from breast openings; ruled out by sterile aspirate and caseous granulomas with rib osteolysis. Primary pulmonary tuberculosis with thoracic wall extension was evaluated, but chest CT showed completely clear lung parenchyma without pulmonary tubercular foci.
case_prompt:
A 21-year-old female from a hilly area of Kashmir presented to a surgical clinic with a 6-year history of persistent pus discharge from two openings on her right breast. The openings had exhibited intermittent spontaneous purulent discharge followed by spontaneous cessation. She experienced no fever, weight loss, night sweats, or other constitutional symptoms, and noted no nipple discharge or nipple retraction. She had previously taken multiple empirical antimicrobial regimens on three occasions, but had been non-adherent and discontinued therapy each time.

On physical examination, systemic examination was normal. Examination of the left breast revealed no abnormality. On the right breast, a 1.5 cm opening was present in the inferior and outer quadrant through which whitish pus was actively discharging, alongside a scarred tract located superiorly that had discharged pus two weeks prior. No palpable breast mass or lump was detected, and there was no axillary lymphadenopathy. Palpation revealed two firm subcutaneous tracts—an inferior tract measuring 4 cm and a superior tract measuring 2.5 cm—both coursing posterosuperiorly and terminating at the fifth rib.

Triage laboratory evaluation showed an elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR). A purified protein derivative (Mantoux) skin test was positive with 16 × 14 mm of induration.

diagnostic_reasoning.candidate: Primary pyogenic breast abscess / Chronic suppurative mastitis
diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Considered primary suspects for chronic discharging sinus tracts of the breast; ruled out because purulent discharge was sterile on conventional and mycobacterial testing and tracts tracked to underlying bone.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: Purulent aspirate was sterile for tubercle bacilli.

diagnostic_reasoning.candidate: Primary pulmonary tuberculosis with chest wall fistulization
diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Considered because most secondary chest wall lesions extend from underlying parenchymal lung disease; excluded by chest CT showing clear lungs without any parenchymal foci.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: Computed tomography scan of chest could not reveal any foci of tuberculosis in lungs; only two sinus tracts in breast tissue and the necrosed rib were seen.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Chest radiography demonstrated an osteolytic lesion in the anterior fifth rib, and surgical excision of the fibrous tracts and 12 cm of necrosed rib confirmed chronic inflammation with areas of caseous necrosis and Langhans giant cells on histopathology.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: Histopathology of specimen was chronic inflammatory cell infiltrate, with areas of caseous necrosis, giant cells (Figure 4).

editor_comments: Secondary tuberculosis of the breast presenting as recurrent discharging mammary sinuses of 6 years' duration originating from contiguous tuberculous osteolysis of the fifth rib without pulmonary parenchymal involvement.
